title: AgentClinic: a multimodal agent benchmark to evaluate AI in simulated clinical environments

bias_targets.methodology: Injecting heuristic flaws (e.g., recency, frequency, confirmation, status quo, false consensus, self-diagnosis) into agent system prompts and measuring the resulting impact on the doctor agent's diagnostic accuracy and the patient agent's post-care ratings.

Prompting the doctor or patient agent to express distrust based on the other party's race, and evaluating the degradation in diagnostic accuracy and simulated patient trust metrics (confidence, compliance, consultation).
Instructing the agent via system prompts to exhibit discomfort or distrust based on the other's gender, followed by measuring the effect on clinical diagnostic accuracy and patient perception scores.
Injecting prompt instructions simulating distrust due to the other agent's sexual orientation, and assessing its impact on diagnostic success and patient evaluation metrics.
Simulating cultural distrust through system prompts and measuring its effect on sequential clinical decision-making, diagnostic accuracy, and patient care ratings.

Prompting agents to distrust the other based on educational background (e.g., an uneducated patient or a doctor from a low-ranked medical school), and tracking the resulting diagnostic accuracy and patient compliance ratings.
Using system prompts to induce discomfort based on the other agent's religious beliefs, then measuring the impact on clinical diagnosis accuracy and the patient agent's reported satisfaction.
Adding prompt context indicating distrust due to the other's socioeconomic background, and assessing its impact on diagnostic accuracy and patient perception.
